summary: This script compares two folders containing bash scripts and finds functions that exist in one folder but not the other. It extracts function names from .sh files in the first folder, compares them side-by-side with the same files in the second folder, and displays the differences in a formatted way with a legend explaining what each type of difference means.

explanations.5: The -eq operator checks if the number of arguments equals 2; the ! negates it, so this line exits if you didn't provide exactly two arguments.
explanations.13: This checks if the sourceFolder doesn't exist as a directory (! -d means 'not a directory'), and if so, prints an error and exits. The && chains commands so they only run if the previous one succeeds.
explanations.16: pushd changes into the sourceFolder and >/dev/null silently discards the directory stack output that would normally print.
explanations.18: printf with escape codes like \e[37;1m sets text color and formatting (white, bold); \e[0;1m resets it. This prints a formatted heading.
explanations.35: This loops through every .sh file in the current directory (which is sourceFolder after pushd).
explanations.36: This checks if the same bash script filename exists in compareWithFolder before trying to compare them.
explanations.37: The parentheses create a subshell, which isolates variable assignments so they don't leak into the main script.
explanations.41: diff compares two inputs side-by-side with a width of 83 characters; --suppress-common-lines hides matching lines.
explanations.42: The <(...) syntax is process substitution — it runs the grep command and feeds its output to diff as if it were a file. grep finds lines starting with 'function', awk extracts just the function name (second field), and sort alphabetizes them.
explanations.43: This pipes the diff output through grep to filter out lines ending with '<' (functions only in the first file), keeping only the differences you want to see.
